jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}日曜日[にちようび]です。
en: Today is Sunday.
why: は names the topic, today, and です says what it is.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}台所[だいどころ]{で|de-place}晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]{を|o-object}作[つく]っています。
en: My mother is making dinner in the kitchen.
why: The person we are talking about, 母, is set up as the topic with は.

jp: 父[ちち]{は|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]六時[ろくじ]{に|ni-time}起[お]きます。
en: My father gets up at six every morning.
why: は sets 父 as the topic that the rest of the sentence describes.

jp: うち{の|no-possessive}犬[いぬ]{は|wa-topic}水[みず]{を|o-object}たくさん飲[の]みます。
en: Our dog drinks a lot of water.
why: The topic 犬 takes は; を is already used for 水, the thing drunk.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}今[いま]二階[にかい]{に|ni-location}います。
en: My older brother is upstairs now.
why: は marks 兄 as the topic whose location is then stated.

jp: 妹[いもうと]{は|wa-topic}七時[しちじ]{に|ni-time}学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: My younger sister goes to school at seven.
why: は makes 妹 the topic; the time and the destination get their own particles.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]{は|wa-topic}庭[にわ]{で|de-place}花[はな]{を|o-object}育[そだ]てています。
en: My grandmother is growing flowers in the garden.
why: The topic is 祖母, marked は, and the rest says what she does.

jp: これ{は|wa-topic}母[はは]{の|no-possessive}かばんです。
en: This is my mother's bag.
why: は marks これ as the topic, and です says what it is.

jp: 夕[ゆう]ご飯[はん]{は|wa-topic}何時[なんじ]です{か|ka-question}。
en: What time is dinner?
why: は sets 夕ご飯 as the topic that the question asks about.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}まだ起[お]きていません。
en: My younger brother isn't up yet.
why: は marks 弟 as the topic; the negative verb then says what is not yet true of him.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}優[やさ]しい人[ひと]です。
en: My mother is a kind person.
why: は marks 母 as the topic being described.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}毎晩[まいばん]十一時[じゅういちじ]{に|ni-time}寝[ね]ます。
en: I go to bed at eleven every night.
why: は marks the speaker as the topic of the daily-routine statement.

jp: 姉[あね]{は|wa-topic}夜[よる]{に|ni-time}本[ほん]{を|o-object}読[よ]みます。
en: My older sister reads books at night.
why: は marks 姉 as the topic; を marks the book she reads.

jp: 祖父[そふ]{は|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]散歩[さんぽ]{を|o-object}します。
en: My grandfather goes for a walk every morning.
why: は marks 祖父 as the topic of the habit that follows.

jp: 父[ちち]{は|wa-topic}会社[かいしゃ]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きました。
en: My father went to the office.
why: は marks 父 as the topic; に or へ marks where he went.

jp: 台所[だいどころ]{は|wa-topic}一階[いっかい]{に|ni-location}あります。
en: The kitchen is on the first floor.
why: は marks 台所 as the topic, and に says where it is.

jp: 猫[ねこ]{は|wa-topic}ソファ{の|no-possessive}上[うえ]{で|de-place}寝[ね]ています。
en: The cat is sleeping on the sofa.
why: は marks 猫 as the topic; で marks where it is sleeping.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}私[わたし]{に|ni-recipient}手紙[てがみ]{を|o-object}書[か]きました。
en: My mother wrote me a letter.
why: は marks 母 as the topic; に marks the person written to.

jp: 父[ちち]{は|wa-topic}弟[おとうと]{に|ni-recipient}自転車[じてんしゃ]{を|o-object}あげました。
en: My father gave my younger brother a bicycle.
why: は marks 父 as the topic who did the giving.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}天気[てんき]{が|ga-subject}いいです{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: The weather is nice today, isn't it?
why: は marks 今日 as the topic, and が marks the thing that is nice.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}ゲーム{が|ga-stative}好[す]きです。
en: My younger brother likes games.
why: は marks 弟 as the topic; が marks the thing he likes.

jp: 姉[あね]{は|wa-topic}歌[うた]{が|ga-stative}上手[じょうず]です。
en: My older sister is good at singing.
why: は marks 姉 as the topic; が marks the skill she has.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}スーパー{で|de-place}野菜[やさい]{を|o-object}買[か]いました。
en: My mother bought vegetables at the supermarket.
why: は marks 母 as the topic who did the shopping.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}電車[でんしゃ]{で|de-means}会社[かいしゃ]{に|ni-destination}通[かよ]っています。
en: My older brother commutes to work by train.
why: は marks 兄 as the topic; で gives the means of travel.

jp: 明日[あした]{は|wa-topic}家族[かぞく]{と|to-with}買[か]い物[もの]{に|ni-purpose}出[で]かけます。
en: Tomorrow I am going out shopping with my family.
why: は marks 明日 as the topic of the plan that follows.

jp: 母[はは]{の|no-possessive}料理[りょうり]{は|wa-topic}とてもおいしいです。
en: My mother's cooking is very delicious.
why: は marks the whole phrase 母の料理 as the topic being praised.

jp: うち{の|no-possessive}庭[にわ]{は|wa-topic}あまり広[ひろ]くないです。
en: Our garden is not very big.
why: は marks 庭 as the topic being described.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]{は|wa-topic}お茶[ちゃ]{を|o-object}飲[の]み{ながら|nagara-while}テレビ{を|o-object}見[み]ています。
en: My grandmother is watching TV while drinking tea.
why: は marks 祖母 as the topic of both actions.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}シャワー{を|o-object}浴[あ]び{て|te-sequence}、朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]{を|o-object}食[た]べます。
en: My older brother takes a shower and then eats breakfast.
why: は marks 兄 as the topic doing both actions in order.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}家[いえ]{で|de-place}宿題[しゅくだい]{を|o-object}します。
en: I do my homework at home.
why: は marks the speaker as the topic of the habit.

jp: お父[とう]さん{は|wa-topic}どこ{に|ni-location}います{か|ka-question}。
en: Where is your father?
why: は marks お父さん as the topic that the question asks about.

jp: 妹[いもうと]さん{は|wa-topic}もう宿題[しゅくだい]{を|o-object}しました{か|ka-question}。
en: Has your younger sister already done her homework?
why: は marks 妹さん as the topic being asked about.

jp: 祖父[そふ]{は|wa-topic}七十歳[ななじゅっさい]です{が|ga-but}、とても元気[げんき]です。
en: My grandfather is seventy, but he is very healthy.
why: は marks 祖父 as the topic being described.

jp: 家族[かぞく]{は|wa-topic}四人[よにん]です。
en: There are four people in my family.
why: は marks 家族 as the topic, and です gives the number.

jp: 私[わたし]{の|no-possessive}部屋[へや]{は|wa-topic}二階[にかい]{に|ni-location}あります。
en: My room is on the second floor.
why: は marks 私の部屋 as the topic whose location is stated.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}もう大学生[だいがくせい]です。
en: My older brother is already a university student.
why: は marks 兄 as the topic being described.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}病院[びょういん]{で|de-place}働[はたら]いています。
en: My mother works at a hospital.
why: は marks 母 as the topic; で marks where she works.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]犬[いぬ]{と|to-with}走[はし]ります。
en: My younger brother goes running with the dog every morning.
why: は marks 弟 as the topic of his morning routine.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}夕方[ゆうがた]{に|ni-time}帰[かえ]ってきます。
en: My mother comes home in the evening.
why: は marks 母 as the topic of the habit that follows.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}朝[あさ]{と|to-and}夜[よる]{に|ni-time}薬[くすり]{を|o-object}飲[の]みます。
en: My mother takes medicine in the morning and at night.
why: は marks 母 as the topic of the routine that follows.

jp: うち{の|no-possessive}猫[ねこ]{は|wa-topic}魚[さかな]{が|ga-stative}大好[だいす]きです。
en: Our cat loves fish.
why: は marks 猫 as the topic; が marks the thing it loves.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}まだ小学生[しょうがくせい]です。
en: My younger brother is still an elementary school student.
why: は marks 弟 as the topic being described.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}いつも早[はや]く起[お]きます。
en: My mother always gets up early.
why: は marks 母 as the topic of the habit that follows.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}夜[よる]遅[おそ]く帰[かえ]ります。
en: My older brother comes home late at night.
why: は marks 兄 as the topic; the verb says what he does.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]{は|wa-topic}毎週[まいしゅう]日曜日[にちようび]{に|ni-time}公園[こうえん]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: My grandmother goes to the park every Sunday.
why: は marks 祖母 as the topic of the weekly habit.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}私[わたし]{に|ni-recipient}「おはよう」{と|to-quote}言[い]いました。
en: My mother said good morning to me.
why: は marks 母 as the topic who spoke.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}母[はは]{の|no-possessive}誕生日[たんじょうび]です。
en: Today is my mother's birthday.
why: は marks 今日 as the topic, and です says what it is.

jp: 明日[あした]{は|wa-topic}雨[あめ]{が|ga-subject}降[ふ]るでしょう。
en: It will probably rain tomorrow.
why: は sets 明日 as the topic; が marks what falls.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}ご飯[はん]{を|o-object}三杯[さんばい]食[た]べました。
en: My older brother ate three bowls of rice.
why: は marks 兄 as the topic; を marks the rice he ate.

jp: 姉[あね]{は|wa-topic}毎日[まいにち]お弁当[べんとう]{を|o-object}持[も]っていきます。
en: My older sister takes a packed lunch every day.
why: は marks 姉 as the topic of the daily habit.

jp: お母[かあ]さん{は|wa-topic}何時[なんじ]{に|ni-time}帰[かえ]ります{か|ka-question}。
en: What time will your mother come home?
why: は marks お母さん as the topic that the question asks about.

jp: 祖父[そふ]{は|wa-topic}リビング{で|de-place}新聞[しんぶん]{を|o-object}読[よ]んでいます。
en: My grandfather is reading the newspaper in the living room.
why: は marks 祖父 as the topic; で marks where he is reading.

jp: 子供[こども]{は|wa-topic}もう寝[ね]ました。
en: The child has already gone to bed.
why: は marks 子供 as the topic; the verb says what happened.

jp: 家[いえ]{は|wa-topic}静[しず]かです。
en: The house is quiet.
why: は marks 家 as the topic being described.

jp: 私[わたし]{の|no-possessive}家族[かぞく]{は|wa-topic}みんな早起[はやお]きです。
en: Everyone in my family is an early riser.
why: は marks 私の家族 as the topic being described.
